1.3 The Initiative shall operate under the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, including the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020, and any subsequent amendments thereto, as applicable to non-governmental organizations.

ARTICLE II: MISSION AND OBJECTIVES

2.1 The mission of the Initiative is to advance community health and well-being through participatory outreach, health education, preventive care, and the strengthening of local health systems.

2.2 The core objectives of the Initiative shall include:

a) To design and implement community-based health programs that address prevalent diseases and health risks, including but not limited to malaria, maternal and child health conditions, waterborne illnesses, and non-communicable diseases.

b) To promote health literacy and behavioral change through culturally appropriate education campaigns, in collaboration with community leaders, religious institutions, and local health workers.

c) To facilitate access to preventive and basic curative health services for underserved populations, including women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities.

d) To support the training and capacity-building of community health volunteers and local health facility staff.

e) To collect, analyze, and disseminate health data to inform program design, policy advocacy, and resource allocation.

f) To forge partnerships with government agencies, development partners, academic institutions, and other civil society organizations in pursuit of shared health objectives.

2.3 The Initiative shall, at all times, operate in a manner consistent with the principles of equity, non-discrimination, transparency, and accountability.

ARTICLE III: GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE

3.1 The Community Health Outreach Initiative (CHOI) operating_region Kwara State, Nigeria. Record status: current.

3.2 Within Kwara State, the Initiative shall prioritize interventions in rural and peri-urban communities, with particular attention to wards and local government areas demonstrating high health vulnerability indicators, limited health facility access, or historically low outreach coverage.

3.3 The Board of Trustees may, by resolution, authorize pilot projects or temporary interventions outside Kwara State, provided such activities are incidental to the core mandate and do not detract from the primary commitment to the State. Any such extension shall be reviewed annually and shall require reauthorization to continue.

3.4 Nothing in this Article shall be construed as limiting the Initiative's ability to participate in national or international advocacy, research dissemination, or knowledge exchange activities that do not involve direct program delivery outside Kwara State.

ARTICLE IV: GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE

4.1 The governance of the Initiative shall be vested in a Board of Trustees, an Executive Management Team, and such committees as the Board may establish from time to time.

4.2 Board of Trustees

a) The Board of Trustees shall be the highest governing body of the Initiative, responsible for overall strategic direction, policy approval, financial oversight, and the appointment of the Executive Director.

b) The Board shall consist of no fewer than seven (7) and no more than eleven (11) members, reflecting a balance of expertise in public health, community development, finance, law, and governance.

c) Trustees shall be appointed for a term of three (3) years, renewable once, provided that no Trustee shall serve more than two consecutive terms. A Trustee who has served two consecutive terms may be re-appointed after a break of at least one term.

d) The Board shall elect from among its members a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson, and a Secretary, each to serve for a term of two (2) years, renewable once.

e) The Board shall meet at least quarterly. Special meetings may be convened by the Chairperson or at the request of at least one-third of the Trustees. Notice of meetings shall be given in writing not less than fourteen (14) days prior to the meeting date.
ARTICLE V: AMENDMENTS AND REVIEW

5.1 This Charter may be amended by a resolution passed by not less than two-thirds (2/3) of the Trustees present and voting at a duly convened meeting of the Board, provided that notice of the proposed amendment has been circulated to all Trustees at least twenty-one (21) days before the date of the meeting.

5.2 Any amendment to Articles I, II, or III of this Charter shall additionally require the approval of the Kwara State Ministry of Health, or its successor agency, before taking effect.

5.3 The Board shall undertake a comprehensive review of this Charter every three (3) years, beginning in 2023, to ensure its continued relevance and alignment with the evolving health needs of the communities served.

5.4 Amendments shall be recorded in the Amendment Log appended to this Charter, with each entry noting the date of adoption, the section affected, a summary of the change, and the effective date.

ARTICLE VI: FUNDING AND FINANCIAL GOVERNANCE

6.1 The Initiative shall maintain a general fund and may establish such special or restricted funds as the Board deems necessary. All funds shall be held in accounts in the name of the Initiative with reputable financial institutions.

6.2 The financial year of the Initiative shall run from the first day of January to the thirty-first day of December in each year.

6.3 The Executive Director, with the assistance of the Finance Committee, shall prepare an annual budget for the approval of the Board. No expenditure shall be made outside the approved budget without prior authorization by the Board or, in cases of urgency, by the Chairperson and Treasurer jointly, subject to ratification at the next Board meeting.

6.4 All income and expenditure shall be recorded in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. The Initiative shall not knowingly accept funds, gifts, or donations from sources whose activities are inconsistent with the values or objectives of the Initiative.

6.5 The Board shall appoint an external auditor annually. The auditor shall examine the accounts of the Initiative and provide a report to the Board and to partners as required.

ARTICLE VII: PARTNERSHIPS AND COLLABORATION

7.1 The Initiative may enter into partnerships, memoranda of understanding, or collaborative agreements with government agencies, non-governmental organizations, academic institutions, community-based organizations, and private sector entities, provided such arrangements advance the objectives set out in Article II.

7.2 All partnership agreements shall be in writing, shall clearly define the roles, responsibilities, and contributions of each party, and shall be reviewed at least every two (2) years.

7.3 The Initiative shall give priority to partnerships that strengthen the capacity of local health workers, community volunteers, and existing health facilities in Kwara State.

7.4 No partnership agreement shall compromise the independence of the Initiative, its commitment to serving the most vulnerable populations, or its accountability to the Board and to the communities it serves.

ARTICLE VIII: REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY

8.1 The Executive Director shall submit to the Board, at each quarterly meeting, a report on the activities, achievements, challenges, and financial position of the Initiative.

8.2 An annual report shall be prepared and made available to stakeholders, including the Kwara State Ministry of Health, local government authorities, community representatives, and funding partners. The annual report shall include a financial statement, a summary of program activities, and an assessment of progress against the strategic plan.

8.3 The Initiative shall maintain records of all program activities, including beneficiary registers, training logs, distribution records, and monitoring and evaluation data. These records shall be kept for a minimum of seven (7) years.

8.4 The Board shall establish a grievance mechanism through which community members and other stakeholders may raise concerns regarding the conduct of any activity, the use of resources, or the behavior of staff and volunteers. All grievances shall be acknowledged within five (5) working days and addressed in accordance with the Board's procedures.

**OUTREACH ACTIVITIES: GENERAL GUIDANCE, REPORTING REQUIREMENTS, AND REVISED TARGETS FOR 2025**

This circular supersedes the guidance issued under File Ref KWMOH/PHC/OUT/2024/118 (dated 14 February 2024) and all subsequent addenda. It consolidates the general compliance requirements for all outreach activities funded or authorised by this Ministry, and incorporates the revised coverage targets for rural health posts as approved by the Honourable Commissioner.

This circular should be read together with the facility-level targets table issued under the same reference (dated 10 March 2025, Section 2). Where any conflict arises between this circular and the facility-level table, the table prevails for coverage calculations, and this circular prevails for all administrative, reporting, and financial compliance matters.

**1. LEGAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE FRAMEWORK**

1.1 All outreach activities must operate under the authority of a valid approval letter issued by this Ministry. Approvals issued in 2023 and 2024 remain valid only until their stated expiry date; no automatic extension is granted. Facilities or implementing partners seeking renewal must submit a formal application at least thirty (30) days before expiry.

1.2 The following documents must be available at the outreach site whenever services are delivered:

- The original approval letter (or a certified true copy);
- A daily activity register signed by the designated team lead;
- The approved microplan for the specific outreach session;
- Cold chain and vaccine management logs, where applicable;
- A copy of this circular.

1.3 Outreach activities must be conducted within the approved catchment area. Any deviation from the approved site location or population served requires prior written approval from the Director of Primary Health Care. Retrospective approvals will not be granted except in emergencies involving risk to life.

**2. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS**

2.1 **Daily Returns.** Every outreach session must generate a daily return using the standard DHIS2 form (Outreach Daily Summary). The return must be submitted electronically to the Local Government Area (LGA) focal person by 5:00 pm on the day of the outreach. Where network connectivity is unavailable, the return must be submitted by SMS to the designated number and the paper form submitted within 48 hours.

2.2 **Monthly Summary Reports.** Each facility must compile a monthly summary of all outreach sessions conducted, disaggregated by service type, age group, sex, and ward. The monthly summary must be submitted by the 3rd working day of the following month to the State Epidemiologist and the LGA Health Authority.

2.3 **Content of Monthly Reports.** The monthly summary must include, at minimum:

- Number of sessions planned vs. conducted;
- Total persons reached per service type;
- Number of defaulters traced and outcomes;
- Adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) reported and investigated;
- Stock balance of vaccines, consumables, and commodities at month end;
- Any community complaints received and how they were resolved;
- Names and designations of all personnel involved.

2.4 **Quarterly Narrative Reports.** A narrative report covering the quarter must be submitted by the 15th of the month following the end of the quarter. The narrative should focus on achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and corrective actions. It should not repeat data already submitted in the monthly returns.

2.5 **Photographic Evidence.** Photographs of outreach sessions must be submitted as an annex to the monthly report. Photographs should be captioned with the date, facility code, and service type. Uncaptioned photographs will not be accepted as evidence of activity.

**3. COVERAGE TARGETS AND MONITORING**

3.1 The approved state target for 2025 is 85 percent coverage for all routine services delivered through outreach. This target applies to all facilities, including those not listed in the facility-level table.

**CHOI PERSONNEL RECORDS — GENERAL POLICIES & PROCEDURES**

**SECTION A: RECRUITMENT AND APPOINTMENT**

A1. All appointments to the Community Health Outreach Initiative (CHOI) shall be made on merit, following a transparent competitive process. Vacancies are advertised through the State Primary Health Care Development Agency notice boards, local professional association channels, and the CHOI internal notice board at the Head Office in Ilorin.

A2. The minimum academic and professional requirements for each cadre are defined in the approved Scheme of Service. No candidate shall be offered employment without presenting verifiable original certificates and current practising licences from the relevant regulatory bodies (NMCN for nurses/midwives, CHPRBN for community health practitioners, and the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria for medical officers where applicable).

A3. All new appointments are subject to a six (6) month probationary period. During probation, the employee's performance is reviewed at the third month and again at the end of the period. Confirmation of appointment is dependent on satisfactory performance, attendance, and conduct. A confirmed appointment is communicated in writing.

A4. Employment contracts are issued in three categories:
- Permanent and pensionable (for staff on the approved establishment)
- Contract (renewable annually, for project-specific roles)
- Volunteer/Intern (without financial remuneration, but with a stipend for transport where funds are available)

A5. All staff, including volunteers, must complete the mandatory onboarding programme within their first month. The programme covers:
- Organisational overview and code of conduct
- Data protection and confidentiality obligations
- Health and safety orientation (including fire drills and emergency evacuation)
- Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) training
- Basic first aid and referral pathways

**SECTION B: LEAVE AND ABSENCE**

B1. Annual Leave
- All confirmed staff are entitled to twenty (20) working days of annual leave per calendar year.
- Leave must be applied for at least two (2) weeks in advance using the standard Leave Request Form (Form HR-04).
- Leave is approved by the immediate supervisor and countersigned by the Head of Human Resources. The Head of Office must approve leave for senior management.
- Annual leave not taken by 31 December is forfeited, except where operational exigencies prevented the leave, in which case it may be carried over with written approval, but not beyond 31 March of the following year.

B2. Sick Leave
- Staff are entitled to twelve (12) working days of fully paid sick leave per year, supported by a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner.
- Absence due to illness beyond the paid entitlement may be covered by unpaid leave or, where applicable, the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) provisions, subject to management discretion.
- For communicable diseases, staff must not resume duty until a medical clearance certificate is presented.

B3. Maternity and Paternity Leave
- Female staff are entitled to sixteen (16) weeks of maternity leave with full pay, in line with the Labour Act and organisational policy.
- Maternity leave may commence not earlier than two weeks before the expected delivery date, unless a medical practitioner advises otherwise.
- Paternity leave of five (5) working days is available to male staff upon the birth of a child, provided the leave is taken within two weeks of the birth.

B4. Compassionate Leave
- Up to five (5) working days of compassionate leave may be granted in the event of the death of a spouse, child, parent, or sibling. Additional days may be approved in exceptional circumstances.
- Compassionate leave is not deducted from annual leave entitlement.

B5. Study Leave
- Study leave with pay may be granted for programmes directly relevant to the employee's role and the organisation's needs, subject to a bonding agreement to serve the organisation for a period equal to the duration of the study leave or as determined by the Board.
- Study leave without pay may be granted for programmes of personal interest, subject to operational requirements.

1.3 The Initiative shall operate under the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, including the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020, and any subsequent amendments thereto, as applicable to non-governmental organizations.

ARTICLE II: MISSION AND OBJECTIVES

2.1 The mission of the Initiative is to advance community health and well-being through participatory outreach, health education, preventive care, and the strengthening of local health systems.

2.2 The core objectives of the Initiative shall include:

a) To design and implement community-based health programs that address prevalent diseases and health risks, including but not limited to malaria, maternal and child health conditions, waterborne illnesses, and non-communicable diseases.

b) To promote health literacy and behavioral change through culturally appropriate education campaigns, in collaboration with community leaders, religious institutions, and local health workers.

c) To facilitate access to preventive and basic curative health services for underserved populations, including women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities.

d) To support the training and capacity-building of community health volunteers and local health facility staff.

e) To collect, analyze, and disseminate health data to inform program design, policy advocacy, and resource allocation.

f) To forge partnerships with government agencies, development partners, academic institutions, and other civil society organizations in pursuit of shared health objectives.

2.3 The Initiative shall, at all times, operate in a manner consistent with the principles of equity, non-discrimination, transparency, and accountability.

ARTICLE III: GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE

3.1 The Community Health Outreach Initiative (CHOI) operating_region Kwara State, Nigeria. Record status: current.

3.2 Within Kwara State, the Initiative shall prioritize interventions in rural and peri-urban communities, with particular attention to wards and local government areas demonstrating high health vulnerability indicators, limited health facility access, or historically low outreach coverage.

3.3 The Board of Trustees may, by resolution, authorize pilot projects or temporary interventions outside Kwara State, provided such activities are incidental to the core mandate and do not detract from the primary commitment to the State. Any such extension shall be reviewed annually and shall require reauthorization to continue.

3.4 Nothing in this Article shall be construed as limiting the Initiative's ability to participate in national or international advocacy, research dissemination, or knowledge exchange activities that do not involve direct program delivery outside Kwara State.

ARTICLE IV: GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE

4.1 The governance of the Initiative shall be vested in a Board of Trustees, an Executive Management Team, and such committees as the Board may establish from time to time.

4.2 Board of Trustees

a) The Board of Trustees shall be the highest governing body of the Initiative, responsible for overall strategic direction, policy approval, financial oversight, and the appointment of the Executive Director.

b) The Board shall consist of no fewer than seven (7) and no more than eleven (11) members, reflecting a balance of expertise in public health, community development, finance, law, and governance.

c) Trustees shall be appointed for a term of three (3) years, renewable once, provided that no Trustee shall serve more than two consecutive terms. A Trustee who has served two consecutive terms may be re-appointed after a break of at least one term.

d) The Board shall elect from among its members a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson, and a Secretary, each to serve for a term of two (2) years, renewable once.

e) The Board shall meet at least quarterly. Special meetings may be convened by the Chairperson or at the request of at least one-third of the Trustees. Notice of meetings shall be given in writing not less than fourteen (14) days prior to the meeting date.

ARTICLE V: AMENDMENTS AND REVIEW

5.1 This Charter may be amended by a resolution passed by not less than two-thirds (2/3) of the Trustees present and voting at a duly convened meeting of the Board, provided that notice of the proposed amendment has been circulated to all Trustees at least twenty-one (21) days before the date of the meeting.

5.2 Any amendment to Articles I, II, or III of this Charter shall additionally require the approval of the Kwara State Ministry of Health, or its successor agency, before taking effect.

5.3 The Board shall undertake a comprehensive review of this Charter every three (3) years, beginning in 2023, to ensure its continued relevance and alignment with the evolving health needs of the communities served.

5.4 Amendments shall be recorded in the Amendment Log appended to this Charter, with each entry noting the date of adoption, the section affected, a summary of the change, and the effective date.

ARTICLE VI: FUNDING AND FINANCIAL GOVERNANCE

6.1 The Initiative shall maintain a general fund and may establish such special or restricted funds as the Board deems necessary. All funds shall be held in accounts in the name of the Initiative with reputable financial institutions.

6.2 The financial year of the Initiative shall run from the first day of January to the thirty-first day of December in each year.

6.3 The Executive Director, with the assistance of the Finance Committee, shall prepare an annual budget for the approval of the Board. No expenditure shall be made outside the approved budget without prior authorization by the Board or, in cases of urgency, by the Chairperson and Treasurer jointly, subject to ratification at the next Board meeting.

6.4 All income and expenditure shall be recorded in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. The Initiative shall not knowingly accept funds, gifts, or donations from sources whose activities are inconsistent with the values or objectives of the Initiative.

6.5 The Board shall appoint an external auditor annually. The auditor shall examine the accounts of the Initiative and provide a report to the Board and to partners as required.

ARTICLE VII: PARTNERSHIPS AND COLLABORATION

7.1 The Initiative may enter into partnerships, memoranda of understanding, or collaborative agreements with government agencies, non-governmental organizations, academic institutions, community-based organizations, and private sector entities, provided such arrangements advance the objectives set out in Article II.

7.2 All partnership agreements shall be in writing, shall clearly define the roles, responsibilities, and contributions of each party, and shall be reviewed at least every two (2) years.

7.3 The Initiative shall give priority to partnerships that strengthen the capacity of local health workers, community volunteers, and existing health facilities in Kwara State.

7.4 No partnership agreement shall compromise the independence of the Initiative, its commitment to serving the most vulnerable populations, or its accountability to the Board and to the communities it serves.

ARTICLE VIII: REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY

8.1 The Executive Director shall submit to the Board, at each quarterly meeting, a report on the activities, achievements, challenges, and financial position of the Initiative.

8.2 An annual report shall be prepared and made available to stakeholders, including the Kwara State Ministry of Health, local government authorities, community representatives, and funding partners. The annual report shall include a financial statement, a summary of program activities, and an assessment of progress against the strategic plan.

8.3 The Initiative shall maintain records of all program activities, including beneficiary registers, training logs, distribution records, and monitoring and evaluation data. These records shall be kept for a minimum of seven (7) years.

8.4 The Board shall establish a grievance mechanism through which community members and other stakeholders may raise concerns regarding the conduct of any activity, the use of resources, or the behavior of staff and volunteers. All grievances shall be acknowledged within five (5) working days and addressed in accordance with the Board's procedures.

It provides the population estimates and derived coverage targets for Rural Health Posts (RHPs) under the direct supervision of the State Ministry of Health. These figures are to be used for planning, resource allocation, and reporting of all outreach activities for the calendar year 2024.

---

**To:** All Local Government Immunization Officers (LGIOs)
All Ward Focal Persons (WFPs)
All Health Facility In-Charges (Rural Health Posts)

**From:** The Director, Primary Health Care and Disease Control

**Subject: Approved Outreach and Target Coverage Rates for 2025 – Vaccination Drive**

This circular supersedes the 2024 outreach targets communicated in Ref. No.
KWMOH/PHC/DI/2024/112 (dated 20 February 2024). All previous target tables,
memoranda, and WhatsApp broadcast messages on 2024 coverage benchmarks are
hereby retired. The 2025 targets take effect from 1 February 2025 and shall
remain valid until 31 January 2026, unless revised by a subsequent circular.

The present document consolidates the approved coverage targets for the
Vaccination Drive and associated routine immunization services across the
state’s rural health posts and outreach clusters. It also restates the
reporting obligations of all officers and facilities.

---

**Section 1: State-Level Target Coverage Rate**

The Kwara State Ministry of Health, in line with the National Primary Health
Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) benchmarks and the State Expanded Programme
on Immunization (SEPI) guidelines, hereby approves the following state-level
target for 2025:

**Vaccination Drive target_coverage_rate 85 percent. Record status: current.**

This rate is the minimum acceptable coverage for all antigens and vaccines
delivered through the Vaccination Drive, including Penta 3, Measles 2, and
the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine for eligible girls. The rate is
current and shall be used for all planning, microplanning, and performance
appraisal in the 2025 calendar year.

All Local Government Areas (LGAs) are required to align their annual
operational plans and quarterly microplans with this target. Where an LGA
has historically performed above the state target, the LGA is encouraged to
maintain its higher performance level, provided that such performance is
sustained and does not draw resources away from underperforming wards.

---

**Section 2: Derived Coverage Targets for Rural Health Posts (2025)**

The following facility-level targets are derived from the approved state
target of 85 percent, adjusted for each facility’s eligible population and
historical performance. These are minimum targets; facilities are encouraged
to exceed them where cold chain capacity and human resources permit.

| 4 | RHP/OMU/001 | Health Education Sessions | 18,000 people | 85% of households (5 persons per household) | 3,060 households |
| 5 | RHP/AJA/002 | Routine Immunization (Penta 3) | 9,400 people | 85% of eligible children | 160 children |
| 6 | RHP/AJA/002 | Antenatal Care (4+ visits) | 9,400 people | 85% of estimated pregnant women | 320 women |
| 7 | RHP/ERI/003 | Routine Immunization (Penta 3) | 7,850 people | 85% of eligible children | 133 children |
| 8 | RHP/ERI/003 | Antenatal Care (4+ visits) | 7,850 people | 85% of estimated pregnant women | 267 women |
| 9 | RHP/IJA/004 | Routine Immunization (Penta 3) | 6,200 people | 85% of eligible children | 105 children |

*Note on rounding:* Facility-level targets are rounded to the nearest whole
number. Where the calculated target is below 5 individuals, the target is
set to 5 for monitoring purposes, to avoid a zero-coverage appearance in
monthly returns.

Program Director (CH-001)
Oversees all CHOI program planning, implementation, and reporting. Represents the organization to government agencies, donors, and community leaders. Directly supervises the Field Coordinators and the Finance Officer. Approves budgets, workplans, and key personnel decisions. Reports to the Board of Trustees.

Field Coordinator, Kwara North (CH-014)
Manages field operations in the Kwara North zone (Jebba, Patigi, Share, Bode Saadu, and surrounding communities). Supervises outreach nurses and community health educators assigned to the zone. Coordinates with local government health offices and traditional leaders. Submits weekly field activity reports to the Program Director.

Finance Officer (CH-020)
Manages all financial records, cash disbursements, and monthly budget tracking. Prepares financial reports for donor submissions. Processes per diem and fuel claims for field staff. Maintains the petty cash register and ensures receipts are filed properly.

Logistics & Supply Officer (CH-022)
Manages medical supply inventory, including vaccines, oral rehydration salts, insecticide-treated nets, and health education materials. Coordinates vehicle maintenance and fuel allocation. Prepares monthly stock reports and raises requests for restocking when supply levels fall below the minimum threshold.

Community Health Educator (CH-028, CH-044, CH-058, CH-064)
Conducts community sensitization sessions on maternal health, child immunization, hygiene, and family planning. Organizes health talks at primary health centers, markets, and community gatherings. Distributes educational materials and collects community feedback for program improvement. Works under the supervision of the Field Coordinator.

Data Clerk (CH-031)
Enters field activity data into the CHOI database. Verifies paper forms for completeness and accuracy. Generates routine counts of outreach sessions, attendees, and referrals. Supports the M&E Officer with data cleaning and basic analysis.

Outreach Nurse (CH-035, CH-061)
Provides basic health services during mobile outreach clinics, including immunization, growth monitoring, antenatal check-ups, and treatment of common childhood illnesses. Refers complicated cases to secondary health facilities. Maintains patient registers and administers vaccines according to the national schedule.

Driver / Field Assistant (CH-040, CH-055)
Transports staff and supplies to field locations. Assists with loading and unloading materials, setting up outreach venues, and mobilizing community members. Performs minor vehicle checks and reports maintenance needs to the Logistics Officer.

Monitoring & Evaluation Officer (CH-047)
Designs data collection tools, conducts field monitoring visits, and compiles quarterly performance reports. Leads the annual community health needs assessment. Supports the Program Director with data for donor reporting.

**CHOI PERSONNEL RECORDS — GENERAL POLICIES & PROCEDURES**

**SECTION A: RECRUITMENT AND APPOINTMENT**

A1. All appointments to the Community Health Outreach Initiative (CHOI) shall be made on merit, following a transparent competitive process. Vacancies are advertised through the State Primary Health Care Development Agency notice boards, local professional association channels, and the CHOI internal notice board at the Head Office in Ilorin.

A2. The minimum academic and professional requirements for each cadre are defined in the approved Scheme of Service. No candidate shall be offered employment without presenting verifiable original certificates and current practising licences from the relevant regulatory bodies (NMCN for nurses/midwives, CHPRBN for community health practitioners, and the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria for medical officers where applicable).

A3. All new appointments are subject to a six (6) month probationary period. During probation, the employee's performance is reviewed at the third month and again at the end of the period. Confirmation of appointment is dependent on satisfactory performance, attendance, and conduct. A confirmed appointment is communicated in writing.

A4. Employment contracts are issued in three categories:
- Permanent and pensionable (for staff on the approved establishment)
- Contract (renewable annually, for project-specific roles)
- Volunteer/Intern (without financial remuneration, but with a stipend for transport where funds are available)

A5. All staff, including volunteers, must complete the mandatory onboarding programme within their first month. The programme covers:
- Organisational overview and code of conduct
- Data protection and confidentiality obligations
- Health and safety orientation (including fire drills and emergency evacuation)
- Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) training
- Basic first aid and referral pathways

**SECTION B: LEAVE AND ABSENCE**

B1. Annual Leave
- All confirmed staff are entitled to twenty (20) working days of annual leave per calendar year.
- Leave must be applied for at least two (2) weeks in advance using the standard Leave Request Form (Form HR-04).
- Leave is approved by the immediate supervisor and countersigned by the Head of Human Resources. The Head of Office must approve leave for senior management.
- Annual leave not taken by 31 December is forfeited, except where operational exigencies prevented the leave, in which case it may be carried over with written approval, but not beyond 31 March of the following year.

B2. Sick Leave
- Staff are entitled to twelve (12) working days of fully paid sick leave per year, supported by a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner.
- Absence due to illness beyond the paid entitlement may be covered by unpaid leave or, where applicable, the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) provisions, subject to management discretion.
- For communicable diseases, staff must not resume duty until a medical clearance certificate is presented.

B3. Maternity and Paternity Leave
- Female staff are entitled to sixteen (16) weeks of maternity leave with full pay, in line with the Labour Act and organisational policy.
- Maternity leave may commence not earlier than two weeks before the expected delivery date, unless a medical practitioner advises otherwise.
- Paternity leave of five (5) working days is available to male staff upon the birth of a child, provided the leave is taken within two weeks of the birth.

B4. Compassionate Leave
- Up to five (5) working days of compassionate leave may be granted in the event of the death of a spouse, child, parent, or sibling. Additional days may be approved in exceptional circumstances.
- Compassionate leave is not deducted from annual leave entitlement.

B5. Study Leave
- Study leave with pay may be granted for programmes directly relevant to the employee's role and the organisation's needs, subject to a bonding agreement to serve the organisation for a period equal to the duration of the study leave or as determined by the Board.
- Study leave without pay may be granted for programmes of personal interest, subject to operational requirements.
